turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll explore the repo structure and search for streaming-related implementation files.Now let's check chat completions and completions.ts, and the lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts / ResponseStream.ts for the streaming helper classes.I now have a complete picture of the streaming architecture. Here's the answer.

## Core streaming implementation

**`src/core/streaming.ts`** — the foundational SSE stream primitive.
- `export class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` (line 21)
- `static fromSSEResponse<Item>(response, controller, client?, synthesizeEventData?)` (line ~31) — parses `Response` body as Server-Sent Events, `JSON.parse`s each `data:` payload, yields items, stops on `[DONE]`, throws `APIError` on error payloads.
- `_iterSSEMessages(response, controller)` (line 219) + `class SSEDecoder` (line 287) — low-level SSE frame decoding, built on `LineDecoder`/`findDoubleNewlineIndex` from `src/internal/decoders/line.ts`.
- `src/streaming.ts` is a deprecated re-export shim: `export * from './core/streaming'`.

**`src/internal/parse.ts`** — the routing point where *every* API response decides whether to stream.
- `defaultParseResponse(client, props)`: if `props.options.stream` is true, it calls either the resource-specific `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (e.g. a custom stream class attached via `__streamClass` in the request options) or falls back to `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` directly. This is the single chokepoint all streaming responses pass through after `fetch()` resolves.

## Higher-level stream helpers (built on `core/streaming.ts`)

- **`src/lib/EventStream.ts`** — `class EventStream<EventTypes>`, a Node-`EventEmitter`-like wrapper (on/off/once/emitted/done/abort) that all the below streaming helpers extend.
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`** — `class ChatCompletionStream<ParsedT> extends AbstractChatCompletionRunner implements AsyncIterable<ChatCompletionChunk>`. Static entry points `createChatCompletion(client, params, options)` and `fromReadableStream(stream)`. Accumulates chunks into a running `ChatCompletionSnapshot` (`finalizeChatCompletion`, line 603).
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`** — `class ChatCompletionStreamingRunner extends ChatCompletionStream`, used for the `runTools` auto-function-calling loop when `stream: true`.
- **`src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts`** — `class ResponseStream<ParsedT> extends EventStream`, static `createResponse(client, body, options)`, accumulates via `accumulateResponse` (`src/lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts`).
- **`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`** — `class AssistantStream extends EventStream`, static `createAssistantStream(threadId, runs, body, options)`, for the (deprecated) Assistants API run streaming.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` (`Responses.create`) | passes `stream: body.stream ?? false` to `this._client.post(...)`, typed `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.stream(body)` | same file, `Responses.stream` | `ResponseStream.createResponse(this._client, body, options)` |
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts` | `stream: body.stream ?? false` → `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(body)` | same file | `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(this._client, body, options)` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(body)` (when `body.stream`) | same file, `Completions.runTools` | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)` |
| `client.completions.create({stream: true})` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts` | `stream: body.stream ?? false` → `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream: true})` | `src/resources/images.ts` | → `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` (also `images.generate` for `ImageGenStreamEvent`) |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream: true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts` | sets `__synthesizeEventData: true`, `stream: body.stream ?? false` → `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream: true})` / `.createAndStream()` (deprecated) / `.stream()` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` | `.stream()`/`.createAndStream()` call `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream(...)` |

All of the `Stream<T>`-typed returns above are resolved inside `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`), whose `.then/.parse()` calls `defaultParseResponse` in `src/internal/parse.ts`, which is the actual dispatch point to `Stream.fromSSEResponse` or a custom `__streamClass`.

## Not verified
- Realtime API (`src/resources/realtime/`, `src/realtime/`, `src/resources/beta/realtime/`) uses WebSockets, not SSE — I confirmed the files exist (`realtime/websocket.ts`, `realtime/ws.ts`) but did not read their internals; it's architecturally separate from the `core/streaming.ts` SSE path.
- `src/resources/audio/speech.ts` streaming (binary audio stream) was not opened — audio streaming likely returns a raw `Response`/`ReadableStream` rather than going through `Stream.fromSSEResponse`, but I didn't confirm this by reading the file.
- I did not execute or test any code — this is a static read of the repository at the `main` branch via `ghx`.

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/
